body:
The web client's pop-up forms — the item form, the ledger entry form, the "New list" box and the admin's delete confirmation — are ordinary page elements dressed up to look like dialogs. Three things a real dialog does are missing:

* Keyboard: pressing Escape does not close them, and Tab does not stay inside the box — it walks off into the page behind, which is still there under the grey overlay.
* Screen readers: they are not announced as dialogs and have no title attached, so a blind user hears a form appear with no explanation of what it is for.
* Focus: when the box opens, focus does not move into it, and when it closes, focus does not return to the button that opened it.

For a mouse user nothing is wrong, which is why it went unnoticed. Fix on the web only: Android's dialogs are real Compose dialogs and already behave correctly.

Simplest route is the browser's native `<dialog>` element, which gives Escape, focus trapping and the announcement for free; the alternative is doing it by hand on the four boxes. Either way the item form needs care, because it already has its own keyboard handling (Enter in the store field adds a chip, the name field has a suggestion list) that must keep working.
title: Web pop-up forms: Escape does nothing, Tab escapes them, screen readers are not told what they are
